prerequisites: Students must have passed at least 60 ECTS credits from basic training module subjects and common industrial branch module subjects (first and second year).
It is highly recommended that students who enroll have passed the first-year course Graphic Expression.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering, specific mechanical technology, which, in accordance with the knowledge acquired as established in section 5 of Ministerial Order CIN/351/2009, aim at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.

Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions, using the models typical of industrial engineering, MECHANICAL SPECIALTY.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge, to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering, MECHANICAL SPECIALTY.
To know, understand, and apply technological and graphic concepts, adapted to new situations, for professional development.
To develop strategies and procedures in solving graphic problems, as a channel for tackling engineering projects.
To use graphic communication among technicians, specified in making and interpreting standardized Industrial Technical Drawing plans, involving new technologies.
To work in a team, developing knowledge with a critical and responsible technical/cultural exchange.
To plan and manage projects in the field of industrial engineering, according to current legislation.

syllabus_topics: FUNDAMENTALS AND METHODOLOGICAL BASES OF INDUSTRIAL DESIGN
Areas of development and application of Industrial Design in Engineering.
STANDARDIZED DEVELOPMENT OF INDUSTRIAL ELEMENTS AND MECHANISMS
Integration into industrial assemblies and functional analysis.
DESIGN, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT OF INDUSTRIAL ELEMENTS AND MECHANISMS USING C.A.D. TOOLS
Design of industrial elements and assemblies, 2D - 3D using CAD.
teaching_methods: Autonomous work using computer and bibliographic resources
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade consists of a written test (60%), practical work (20%), and team assignments (20%). The written test is exclusionary; students must pass it to pass the course. Those who renounce continuous assessment will be evaluated by a final exam system where a score above 50% is required in each of three parts: written test (60%), practical test (20%), and team work test (20%). For the extraordinary call, evaluation is exclusively through the final assessment system, which includes a written test (60%, mandatory pass), a practical test (20%), and a team work test (20%). For the practical and team work tests in the extraordinary call, the scores obtained during the course will be maintained if the student does not take the extraordinary tests.
